content:
Clara: Hey folks — posting the updated mock for the Alerting & SLO config panel. Main asks: make thresholds clearer, notification channel UX less modal-y, and a preview flow for suppression rules. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/alerting-ui

Tom: Nice — I like the compact rows. Two quick questions: 1) how do we show whether a threshold is absolute vs. relative? 2) can we preview the exact notification payload? :thinking_face:

Samir: For (1) I'd suggest a small pill next to threshold: "avg" / "% of baseline". Keeps the label short. For (2) yes — show a toggle "Preview payload" that expands a JSON snippet. Example below:

```json
{"alert_name":"high_latency","threshold":200,"unit":"ms","channel":"pagerduty","message":"{{service}} p50 > 200ms"}
```

Priya: UX nit: the current "Add suppression" button is buried in the kebab. Can we make suppression a first-class card under each rule? Users frequently apply time-based suppressions during maintenance windows. :wrench:

Ava: Accessibility: color contrast for the green "OK" badge is borderline (WCAG AA). Also keyboard users need a clear focus state on the channel selector. Suggest: 2px solid focus ring and ensure badges use >= 4.5:1 contrast.

Clara: Good calls. On the suppression card idea — what about a small inline timeline UI: "Suppress for X hours / until end of maintenance" with quick presets and a detailed modal for advanced rules? That keeps the main flow light.

Tom: Love presets. One more copy tweak: change "Notify via" to "Send alert to" — more action-oriented and reads better in sentences. Thoughts? :memo:

Samir: "Send alert to" reads fine. Also propose adding a small muted helper text under the channel selector: "Channels are tried in order; failures fallback to email." Could help with our multi-channel routing customers.

Priya: Regarding preview: add an inline "Test delivery" button that simulates an alert (with safe sandbox delivery to a test webhook). Label it: "Send test alert (no escalation)" so it's clear. CS asked for that during onboarding. @CS-Bot can confirm expected behavior?

CS-Bot: Confirmed: customers request non-escalating test sends a lot. Should default to send-to-test-channel and log an audit entry. :white_check_mark:

Ava: Also flag: all modals must trap focus and include an "Esc closes" affordance. The suppression presets should be selectable via keyboard-only.

Clara: UX question for engineers: can we render the payload preview with token substitution ({{service}}, {{env}}) and toggle a sample data set? That would make the preview actually useful.

Samir: Yes — we can provide a "sample context" dropdown. Backend returns rendered preview by running templating in a sandbox. We should cache results for the same context to avoid compute spikes.

Tom: Flow idea: inline rule row -> expand -> preview pane (left) + suppression card (right) + channel order drag handle. That minimizes modals and surfaces common actions.

Priya: One more microcopy: change "Suppression window" to "Silence window"? "Suppression" is a bit jargony for CS-facing docs. "Silence" is more standard in ops tooling.

Ava: "Silence" is clearer, but ensure we update aria-labels and tooltips accordingly. Also add a status text for assistive tech when a rule is silenced: "Rule X silenced until 2026-05-01 02:00 UTC".

Clara: These are great. Next steps: I'll iterate the mock with: pill for absolute/relative, inline preview JSON + "Send test alert" button, suppression card with presets, rename to "Silence window", and accessibility updates. I'll post version 2 tomorrow. :sparkles:

Tom: :thumbsup: Please include copy variants so we can A/B test "Send alert to" vs "Notify" in the console.

Samir: FYI engineering: we'll need an endpoint for test deliveries and a rendered-preview endpoint. I'll open an RFC and link it here.

Clara: Thanks team — last call for anything else?

Priya: Add audit log row for suppression creation/deletion. Small customers ask for this for compliance.

Ava: And keyboard shortcut cheat-sheet: pressing "s" while focused on a rule toggles silence. Could be useful for power users.

Clara: Great — adding everything. I'll ping again with v2 and a short usability checklist. :eyes:
